messages.subject: Some observations disappear results / estimates
parts:
Hi,

sorry if this is a very simple error or question, but I don't seem to be able to solve it myself.

I am using Distance in R to estimate the density and abundance of endangered lizards in three different locations. I want to use a common detection function, since I don't have any sound hypothesis to believe that the detection function is different among sites, and in fact in two of the three sites have very few sightings for the moment.

Therefore, I entered the data including three regions and and all the corresponding samples, using obs_table, sample_table, region_table.

The distribution of observations per site is as follows:
Finestrelles      Forques        Pleta
          39               4                     5

and my code is simply (I attach the four pieces of data):

ds(data=disdata,
               obs_table = obs_table,
               sample_table = sample_table,
               region_table = region_table,
               transect = "line")

However, the surprise for me is when the results suggest that the density and abundance for the two last locations is... zero! Which is obviously impossible since at least there is an abundance of 4 and 5. The problem seems to be that the even though the analysis ackowledges that I entered 48 observations, it is not detecting/using the observations of the two last locations to calculate their results... that is (see below in bold) the number of observations in the distance analysis is 48, but then th total is only 39 (including only the observations for the first population) in the tables of results. This leaves the other two populations as if there were no sigthings of lizards and an estimate of 0.

So, I am not able to understand the results... perhaps I am missing something, is it a problem of the low number of sightings?

Any help will be much appreciated.

Eudald

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Some observations disappear results / estimates
parts:
Eudald

Thanks for sending along all the components of your distance sampling data.  The problem that you detected arose because your perpendicular distances appear in disdata​ and in that file you have those distances associated with sequential values (1, 2, 3, ..., 48) in the field X​.  In obs_table​ you had the field object​ that contained values up to 66, with 18 values missing (resulting in 48 records in the file).  When the software tried to find distances for objects​ numbered > 48, it could find none.  The objects numbered > 48 all fell into the strata Forques and Pleta; hence the function had no distances to assign to those strata.

There needs to be a connection between the information in disdata​ and obs_table​.  The way I made this happen was to replace the object​ values in obs_table​ with the sequential values in the field X​.  You can see what I did in the following code:

library(Distance)
setwd("E:/troubleshoot/Eudald")
disdata <- read.csv("distance_data.csv")
obs_table <- read.csv("obs_table.csv")
region_table <- read.csv("region_table.csv")
region_table$Area <- region_table$Area / 10000 # convert to hectares
sample_table <- read.csv("sample_table.csv")
# re-define the Obs table field "object" to point to the sequential numbers
obs_table$object <- NULL
obs_table$object <- obs_table$X
# make a unit conversion so density is per hectare
convunit <- convert_units("meter", "meter", "hectare")
out <- ds(data=disdata,

obs_table = obs_table,
   sample_table = sample_table,
   region_table = region_table,

transect = "line",
   convert_units = convunit)
summary(out)

Note that I also made some adjustments to the Area units such that the output would produce density estimates in lizards per hectare rather than lizards per sq. meter.

Recognise the challenge of having few detections in the later two strata.  The shape of the detection function is driven by the 39 detections in Finestrelles.  I note you had double the effort in the later two strata compared to Finestrelles, but were still only able to produce 4 and 5 detections respectively.  You should be cautious in your presentation of the estimates from the later two strata; note the uncertainty in the estimates for those strata is large (CV>0.4)

Thank you very much Eric!

I knew it was going to be some kind of absurd mistake, I has already checked the names of samples and regions but it didn't occur to me to check the numeration of the observations. This mismatch happened simply because I deleted the data on other reptiles from the original database.

You are right in that we have too few detections in the later two strata, in fact we are planning on going twice again, we are in time to do it, we are just doing the field work now. Comments on that were much appreciated, as well as the script! Thanks for the troubleshooting!

E
